note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.

admission.contract: registry/tree agreement, both ways (an unregistered check file is dead code, a registered file that does not exist is a dangling entry), plus admission-shape validation: every registered entry carries a non-empty admission record — the contracts this file's own note declares and nothing else carries
admission.removal_signal: a suite runner whose discovery is registry-driven, making an unregistered file unrunnable by construction — constrain-generation subsumes this detection

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive); the embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation
admission.removal_signal: a gateway-side consumer receipt surface that reports served consultations back to the consumer — that would verify against the server's record rather than the consumer's claim, superseding this check's weaker evidence

admission.contract: the client kit's install guarantees, fired rather than merely written: fresh-install layout, idempotency, the one-line degrade at exit 11, the pinless-body deny, harness-loadable skill frontmatter, the entry-2 boundary (no kit tool reads gateway state), and the absence of any colocation default. Registered because a test nothing invokes is the orphan-guard shape kogaki#6 was filed to end
admission.removal_signal: the kit's separation into its own repository (fires on a second installing consumer, per kogaki#9) — the test goes with it and this repo stops being its home

admission.contract: the owner-facing proposal contract as a record shape (manifest item 3, specs/SPEC.md:97-98): Where/Why with the computed premise's negation offered as a first-class option, machine-proposed options plus an UNCONDITIONAL free-text override, payload capture (options offered + answer, never the answer alone), and the non-member fallback of specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md:76-86 — an act in neither the navigation nor the proposal list is a report, never a silent classification. Carries the effect-stating property's FORM floor only and says so in its own output; sufficiency is judgment and routes to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: a second consumer whose proposals differ in shape from Terrain's — the record schema was specced against one implementation, so a second one is the evaluation of the shape, not a widening of it: either the schema generalizes (and this check moves to it) or the contract splits per consumer and this file, which validates a single shape, is the wrong carrier

admission.contract: the gate carrier (manifest item 4, specs/SPEC.md:99-101): the declared gate registry as the enumeration a coverage claim is a fraction OF, the MEDIUM BINDING (a Claude Code host renders a gate through the selector affordance and never prose — the one form of the legibility rule that is falsifiable), AskUserQuestion tool-use evidence beside every captured answer, payload/answer capture including the GATE-LESS row no suite upstream held, and the machine's own comparison (ranked recommendation, per-option evidence, overturning evidence, no pre-selection) sited here rather than in item 3. Its reporting carries the three-part crash remedy: guarded rows, CANNOT-DETERMINE rendered separately from FAIL so a crash is never spent as a positive finding, and repetition disclosed as one deterministic cause rather than N confirmations. Shares no machinery with check-proposal-contract.sh, which binds a record and by its own decision delivers no rendering. Carries the comparison's STRUCTURE only and says so in its own output; whether the evidence is the evidence bearing on an option, and whether a gate reads as a gate beyond its named affordance, are judgment and route to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: a harness-side carrier that enforces the medium binding at the moment a gate is raised — a Stop or PostToolUse hook reading AskUserQuestion tool-use evidence directly (topics/claude-code-ops.md:35@5f769dfe names the transcript/tool-call layer as never exercised). That would verify against the host's own record rather than against a declared registry and a committed capture file, and constrain-generation subsumes after-the-fact detection: this check goes when it lands

admission.contract: Terrain's three ported contracts over every survey record in the tree (manifest item 1, specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §2): completeness as a cover counted in placements — every Strand placed, no-relation Strands in an explicit named section, nothing silently dropped; the figure counted AFTER composition, recomputed here from the placements themselves, naming which family it counted; and navigation state carrying no narrowing key, so a survey record cannot smuggle the refused minimal-form bundling in as a field — plus the seam pin on every record. The detection half behind terrain/terrain.mjs's generation-time refusal (validateSurvey applies the same schema-carried rules before writing); the fixture pass is the evidence both halves discriminate. Carries composition FACTS only and says so in its own output; whether the grouping axis serves the owner and whether a ratified narrowing was worth taking are judgment and route to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: terrain/terrain.mjs validateSurvey becoming the registry-verified SOLE writer of survey records, with the fixture pass exercising the mjs validator directly rather than this mirror — once no unvalidated write path exists, constrain-generation subsumes after-the-fact detection, the same shape the registry meta-check's own removal signal ratified (kogaki#2)
